headline: High: Rasa can ingest and transmit conversational content while godot_rl_agents is a non-networked game agent, creating default data-leakage and compliance risk if paired through shared inputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: godot_rl_agents has no documented I/O surfaces and no network egress, so it cannot directly inject Rasa. Rasa exposes many chat channels and can ingest user text, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel or parser bridge. The only plausible pathway is unusual manual copy-paste or external orchestration, so risk stays low.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies godot_rl_agents output into a Rasa channel as instructions, injection becomes possible.
IF an external orchestrator bridges the two through a shared file or message queue, Rasa may parse attacker-controlled text.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate channels with no copy-paste bridge.
Prefix all transferred text as data, not instructions.
Add a human review step before any Rasa action.
Use a fixed schema for inter-agent messages.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all shared messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Rasa can receive text and voice and has allowlisted network egress, so any sensitive content it sees may leave the local boundary. godot_rl_agents is non-networked, but if its outputs are shared into Rasa, the pair can leak data through Rasa's external channels. The interaction is inferred from documented surfaces, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF godot_rl_agents outputs are copied into Rasa conversations, those contents can be transmitted onward.
IF Rasa is connected to any listed API channel, text or voice content may traverse third-party services.
mitigations: Do not route sensitive content into Rasa.
Disable or isolate external API channels during testing.
Redact secrets before any handoff.
Use a local-only staging bot for transfers.
requires-engineering: enforce per-channel data-loss prevention.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: godot_rl_agents has no documented write surfaces, while Rasa supports multiple external chat APIs but no filesystem or git write capability is shown. There is no clear overlapping mutable resource, and Rasa cannot run multiple instances. Any conflict would require extra orchestration not present in the profiles, so low fits.
conditions: IF both agents are wired to the same mutable external resource, write contention can occur.
IF an orchestrator adds shared filesystem writes, conflict risk increases.
mitigations: Avoid shared writable resources.
Run only one Rasa instance per resource.
Separate test and production channels.
Use explicit locking in any orchestrator.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: godot_rl_agents can generate outputs that an operator may feed into Rasa, and Rasa can then act on conversational inputs across multiple channels. Because no verification step is documented between them, mistaken game-agent output could cascade into customer-facing responses. The pathway is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF godot_rl_agents output is treated as authoritative by a Rasa workflow, downstream responses may be wrong.
IF Rasa is configured to trigger actions from conversation text, errors can propagate to users.
mitigations: Require human review before Rasa sends replies.
Add validation rules for any imported text.
Limit Rasa actions to safe, reversible operations.
Log source provenance for transferred content.
requires-engineering: implement confidence gating between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: godot_rl_agents is open-source, non-networked, and touches no data classes, while Rasa handles text and voice and can connect to third-party APIs. No explicit residency or certification mismatch is documented, so only a limited compliance gap is visible: if sensitive conversational data is routed into Rasa channels, retention and third-party exposure concerns arise. The other agent is not cited for residency because it has none documented.
conditions: IF regulated text or voice data is sent through Rasa channels, compliance obligations may apply.
IF a deployment requires strict local-only processing, Rasa's external APIs violate that requirement.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Rasa channels.
Disable third-party connectors for regulated workflows.
Document retention settings for each channel.
Review data-processing agreements before deployment.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
